analysis.investment_thesis: Aequs is a loss-making, debt-laden contract manufacturer with negative operating margins and deeply negative free cash flow — it fails every core criterion I use before I even look at the business. At 1,140x forward P/E on a company burning cash, the market is pricing in a transformation that has not arrived in three years of trying.
key_strengths: Promoter holding at 59% is stable — no stake reduction visible
Gross margin of 56% suggests embedded value-add in manufacturing, not pure commoditized work
Aerospace sector has structural tailwinds from India's defense indigenisation push (PLI, offset policies)
key_risks: Debt-to-Equity of 1.08 — more than 3x my hard ceiling of 0.3; finance costs of ₹64 Cr annually on thin/negative EBITDA is existential
Free cash flow of -₹239 Cr in FY25 (worsening each year); capex of ₹265 Cr with CWIP at ₹395 Cr means cash burn will continue before any return
Revenue declined from ₹965 Cr to ₹925 Cr in FY25 while net losses widened back to -₹102 Cr — the FY24 improvement was a blip, not a trend
red_flags: Three consecutive years of net losses: -₹110 Cr, -₹14 Cr, -₹102 Cr — no consistent earnings, zero dividend history
Operating margin of -1.84% in FY25 despite a 56% gross margin signals massive overhead and SG&A bloat that management has not controlled
Other income swung to -₹6 Cr in FY25 from +₹44 Cr in FY24 — underlying operating business is weaker than headline EBITDA suggested
Valuation of 288x EV/EBITDA and 12.85x P/B for a loss-making company is irrational speculation, not investing
analysis.detailed_analysis:
From my lens, this business fails at the first filter: the balance sheet. A D/E of 1.08 with ₹785 Cr in borrowings and ₹64 Cr in annual finance costs is a company living on a banker's sufferance, not on the strength of its own earnings. I built DMart on the principle that you never let debt dictate your operating decisions — Aequs has no such luxury. The free cash flow of -₹239 Cr in FY25 with capex of ₹265 Cr and CWIP of ₹395 Cr tells me the investment cycle is far from over, and equity holders are funding it at a very high price with no certainty of returns.

The diversification across aerospace, toys, and consumer durables sounds like optionality, but to me it reads as a business still searching for its identity after 25 years. The gross margin of 56% is intriguing — there is real manufacturing capability here — but EBITDA collapsed from ₹163 Cr in FY24 to ₹57 Cr in FY25 with revenue actually shrinking, which means overhead is not under control. I would need to see three years of consistent positive operating cash flow, net profit, and D/E below 0.3 before I even begin to evaluate the business model. Until then, I would rather sit on cash than own this at any price, let alone at 1,140x forward earnings.
